name: French Marquise
outline: Pointed boat-shaped marquise outline with two points.
end_treatment: Pointed, finished with French tips: several small facets at each point instead of one large facet, which reinforce the point and add flash.
durability_notes: Still a pointed marquise. The French tips reinforce the most fragile part of the stone, but the points remain the area most likely to chip.

provenance.claim_scope: We publish this plain, repeatable definition of the French Marquise and cut these stones in-house. The French in the name refers to the tip faceting technique, not a separate shape.
provenance.claim_boundary: We did not invent French tip faceting, which is an established marquise finishing technique, nor do we hold a patent or trademark on the term French Marquise.

sources.claim: A French tip is several small facets at the point of a marquise, pear, or heart, used to reinforce the fragile tip and add flash.
sources.source: International Gem Society, history of marquise diamonds

sources.claim: On a grading report a French Marquise is described as a marquise brilliant; the French refers to the tip faceting, not a separate shape.
sources.source: General rule of grading laboratories: reports certify geometry, not finishing trade names.
